seo.title: Security - Where EagleEye runs, what it reads and what leaves your tenant
seo.description: EagleEye runs inside your own Azure subscription and Entra tenant. This page lists every resource, every Graph permission, every data flow, and the 3 calls that reach SSW.

title: Security - Where EagleEye runs, what it reads and what leaves your tenant

pageBlocks.byLine: EagleEye is an Azure Managed Application you install from Azure Marketplace into your own subscription and Entra tenant. Your email is read, analysed and stored there. SSW never receives it. This page says what runs where, what leaves your tenant, and what we have not built yet.

pageBlocks.body:
## Where everything runs

The Marketplace install creates 1 managed resource group in your subscription, named `mrg-ssweagleeye-xxx`. Every Azure resource below lives in it. The 3 app registrations in the Identity row are the exception: they are objects in your Entra tenant, outside the resource group. You own the subscription, the bill and the access policies.

| Component | Azure resource | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Portal | Container App `ca-nextjs-xxx` | Sign in with Entra ID, manage tags and prompts, run scans, view reports |
| API | Container App `ca-api-xxx` | Backend between the Portal and your database |
| Scan jobs | Container Apps Jobs `cj-cli-xxx` (nightly) and `cj-manual-xxx` (on demand) | Read mailboxes and GitHub, apply tags, write results |
| Database | Azure SQL `db-shared-xxx` | Stores scan results. Power BI connects here with a read-only login |
| AI model | Azure OpenAI `openai-shared-xxx`, with a chat model you deploy under the name `eagleeye` | Runs your AI tag prompts. It is your resource, your quota and nobody else's traffic |
| Secrets | Key Vault `kv-shared-xxx` | App registration secrets, connection strings, the Azure OpenAI key, the GitHub App private key |
| Monitoring | Application Insights and Log Analytics `ai-shared-xxx` | Logs and metrics, kept for 30 days |
| Identity | 3 app registrations in your tenant: `SSW.EagleEye.Engine`, `SSW.EagleEye.Api`, `SSW.EagleEye.Portal` | Created at install by a Master app that you own and can delete afterwards |

### Region

Every resource is created in the region of the resource group you pick in the Marketplace wizard, with one exception: the Azure OpenAI account is currently created in East US, because that region has the broadest model catalogue. Making the Azure OpenAI region customer-selectable is in progress. Until it ships, AI tag prompts, which include email text, are processed in East US. Rule-based tags never call the model and never leave your region.

## Data flow

| Data | Where it comes from | Sent to Azure OpenAI? | Stored in your database? | Kept until |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Email subject, sender, To, CC and BCC, sent date, message and conversation IDs | Microsoft Graph, for the mailboxes of the members of the Entra group you configure | No. For *AI with mentions* tags the display names of the sender and recipients are sent so the model can match a mention to a person | Yes. Subject is capped at 256 characters | You delete it |
| Email body, as plain text | Microsoft Graph, requested as text, not HTML | Only for AI tags, and only when the tag has AI enabled. Mail from external senders reaches the model only when the tag's *scan external emails with AI* option is on | **No.** The body is held in memory for the duration of the scan and discarded. The `Message` table has no body column. The model's short supporting quote for a tag match (up to 4,000 characters) is stored with the match | You delete it, or a rescan replaces it |
| Attachments | Not fetched | No | No | n/a |
| Calendar invitations that arrive in a mailbox | Microsoft Graph, same call as email | Same rules as email | Same fields as email, stored as email | You delete it |
| People: display name, email address, internal or external, active or not | Microsoft Graph directory | Display names only, for mention tags | Yes | You delete it |
| GitHub issues and pull requests (optional) | A GitHub App you install on your own organization | Title and body, for AI tags only | Title, author, assignees, reviewers and approvals, open, closed and merged dates, repository, number and URL. Issue and pull request bodies are not stored | You delete it |
| Tags, rules and prompts | You, in the Portal | The prompt is sent with every AI request for that tag | Yes | You archive them |
| Webhook payloads | EagleEye, when a tag matches | No | No. Sent to the endpoint you configure, and written to your Application Insights logs | 30 days in logs |
| Logs and metrics | API, Portal and jobs | No | Application Insights in your subscription | 30 days |
| Secrets | Key Vault in your subscription | No | Key Vault | Soft-delete for 90 days after deletion |

There is no automatic purge. The database is yours, so the retention period is whatever you decide, and deleting the managed application removes all of it (see *Deleting your data*).

## What leaves your tenant

Three calls reach infrastructure that SSW hosts. None of them carries email, people or tag data; they carry only what any HTTPS request carries, your deployment's IP address and a user agent.

| Call | Endpoint | When | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Container image pull token | `https://api.ssweagleeye.com/api/acr/credentials` | During install, and when you apply an update | Lets your subscription pull the EagleEye images |
| Container images | SSW's Azure Container Registry | During install and updates | The Portal, API and job images |
| Version manifest | `https://ssweagleeye.blob.core.windows.net/version-manifests/version.json` | When a signed-in user opens the Portal (at most once a day per browser), and when someone checks for or starts an update | Tells the Portal whether a newer release is available |

Scans never call the version manifest. Each release ships with its own support end date inside the image. When the installed release passes that date, scans pause and the Portal says so; they resume once you apply the update. If the version manifest is unreachable, the Portal cannot offer or start an update, but scans, sign-in, reports and tags keep working.

Two more things to know:

* The Portal loads Google Analytics and Plausible on every page, including signed-in pages. They record page views, page URLs and browser details, and are not configured to collect email content or report data. A page URL can include report filters. To turn them off, block `googletagmanager.com` and `plausible.io` in your browsers or on your network.
* Calls to Microsoft Graph, Azure OpenAI and GitHub go directly from your subscription to those services, under your own agreements with Microsoft and GitHub. SSW is not in the path.

Updates are built by SSW's CI pipeline, published through Azure Marketplace, and applied when you click *Update now* in the Portal. SSW cannot push code into your subscription.

## Microsoft Graph permissions

EagleEye uses 2 sets of permissions: one for the install, one at runtime.

### Install only: the Master app

You create this app registration yourself and grant it these **application** permissions so the Marketplace deployment can create the 3 runtime apps without a human clicking through consent screens. [Delete it after the install](/docs/delete-master-app); nothing at runtime uses it.

| Permission | Why it is needed |
| --- | --- |
| `Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy` | Create and update the Engine, API and Portal app registrations |
| `AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All` | Grant the Engine app its Graph permissions |
| `DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All` | Grant the Portal delegated access to the API |
| `Domain.Read.All` | Read your tenant's email domains so EagleEye can tell internal from external senders |
| `Group.Read.All` | Find the Entra group you chose and assign it to the Portal |

### Runtime: the Engine app

| Permission | Type | Why it is needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Mail.Read` | Application | Read the mailboxes of the members of the configured group. Microsoft grants this permission tenant-wide; EagleEye only reads group members. You can narrow it to specific mailboxes with an Exchange Online application access policy |
| `User.Read.All` | Application | Resolve names and addresses, and mark people as internal or external and active or inactive |
| `GroupMember.Read.All` | Application | List the members of the configured group, which is the list of mailboxes to scan |

### Runtime: the Portal app

| Permission | Type | Why it is needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `User.Read` | Delegated | Sign the user in and show their name |
| `access_as_user` on `SSW.EagleEye.Api` | Delegated | Call the EagleEye API as the signed-in user |

The full reference, including what each of the 3 apps does, is in [App Registrations & Permissions](/docs/app-registrations-reference).

## Access control

* **Sign-in** is Entra ID only, pinned to your tenant. Your Conditional Access and MFA policies apply because it is your tenant.
* **Who can get in** is one Entra security group you choose at install. Nobody outside the group can open the Portal.
* **What they can do**: today every member of that group has the same, full access, including tags, prompts, scans and settings. Separate roles for viewers and administrators are on the roadmap and not available yet.
* **Power BI** connects with a read-only SQL login that you manage in Key Vault.

## Encryption, network and secrets

* **In transit**: the Portal and API are served over HTTPS by Container Apps. Calls to Microsoft Graph, Azure OpenAI and GitHub use TLS.
* **At rest**: Azure SQL encrypts the database with transparent data encryption using a Microsoft-managed key, the Azure default. Key Vault holds every secret. Customer-managed keys are not supported yet.
* **Network**: the Portal, API, SQL server and Azure OpenAI account use public Azure endpoints protected by Entra authentication and keys. The SQL server allows connections from Azure services. Private endpoints and virtual network integration are not available yet.
* **Secrets you own and rotate**: the Engine and Portal client secrets and the database logins. The runbooks are [Manage Secrets for App Registrations](/docs/secret-management-app-registrations) and [Manage Credentials for Database](/docs/manage-database-credentials).

## Deleting your data

Delete the managed application, or the resource group that contains it, and the database, Key Vault and logs go with it. The 3 app registrations do not, because they live in your Entra tenant. Until you delete them, the Engine app keeps its `Mail.Read` permission. Delete `SSW.EagleEye.Engine`, `SSW.EagleEye.Api` and `SSW.EagleEye.Portal`, and the Master app if you kept it, under **App registrations** in the Azure portal, as described in [Cleanup before Redeployment](/docs/redeploy-cleanup). There is no copy at SSW to ask us to delete. Deleting a single person's data from a live installation is a manual database operation today; ask support and we will walk you through it.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Email [security@ssw.com.au](mailto:security@ssw.com.au). Our PGP key and disclosure details are in [security.txt](/.well-known/security.txt), published per RFC 9116.

## What we have not done yet

We would rather you read this here than find it in a questionnaire.

* We do not hold a SOC 2 report or an ISO 27001 certificate for EagleEye, and we have not published a third-party penetration test. Ask us and we will tell you where each one stands.
* Azure OpenAI region selection at install is in progress; today the account is created in East US.
* There is no customer-visible audit log of who changed a tag, prompt or setting, only created and modified stamps on each record.
* There are no roles inside the Portal; group membership grants full access.
* No private networking and no customer-managed keys.

Security questionnaires go to [security@ssw.com.au](mailto:security@ssw.com.au). We aim to return a completed questionnaire within 10 business days.
